stateFarmReturning.overview: I explored how a returning-customer homepage could help people resume an unfinished auto quote with less effort. decisionStory.title: Make returning feel like continuing.
decisionStory.problem: A customer with an unfinished quote needs to recognize where they left off and find the next action without navigating the site again.
decisionStory.decision: I made the saved quote and continuation action prominent on the homepage, supported by contextual recommendations and a Digital Assistant entry point.
decisionStory.result: A returning-customer homepage prototype that makes quote continuation visible and connects the next step with relevant guidance.
decisionStory.note: This is a prototype direction. Quote-completion and conversion improvements have not been measured here.

continuation.title: Pick Up Where You Left Off. Smarter.
continuation.intro: Reimagined the returning-customer experience by bringing quote continuation, AI-powered personalization, and contextual guidance into one seamless journey across Auto, Home, and Renters insurance.
continuation.rationale: Rather than forcing customers to restart or navigate disconnected experiences, the prototype explored how embedded AI could recognize customer intent, restore progress, and recommend the most relevant next action.
continuation.problem: Traditional quoting experiences can create friction when customers leave and return. Repeated questions, disconnected journeys, and limited contextual guidance increase cognitive effort and introduce opportunities for abandonment.
continuation.experienceIntro: Designed an intelligent continuation experience centered on four capabilities. Explore each stage to see the capability behind it.

stages.title: Recognize
stages.subtitle: Returning customer
stages.description: Tailor content, guidance, and coverage options to known customer information and intent.

stages.title: Restore
stages.subtitle: Saved progress
stages.description: Surface saved quote progress and guide customers directly to their next step.

stages.title: Guide
stages.subtitle: Contextual AI
stages.description: Provide contextual support directly within the quoting experience instead of requiring a separate chatbot.

stages.title: Continue
stages.subtitle: Next best action
stages.description: Allow customers to review, edit, and confirm information before continuing.

decisions.title: Continuity over repetition.
decisions.description: Prioritized saved progress and contextual next steps over restarting the journey.

decisions.title: Guidance over complexity.
decisions.description: Simplified insurance decisions through progressive disclosure and relevant assistance.

decisions.title: Intelligence over automation.
decisions.description: Introduced helpful AI recommendations while keeping customers in control.

continuation.contribution: Led UX strategy, experience architecture, interaction design, and high-fidelity prototyping. Connected research insights with AI maturity goals to explore a scalable continuation experience and align cross-functional teams on future product direction.
continuation.intendedImpact: Reduce unnecessary steps, increase quote completion opportunities, strengthen customer confidence, and establish a foundation for more predictive and agentic insurance experiences.
continuation.impactTitle: From Disconnected Quotes to Intelligent Continuity
continuation.impactStatement: Shifted the experience from repetitive, transactional interactions toward context-aware guidance—demonstrating how personalization and embedded AI could simplify quote completion while laying the groundwork for proactive insurance assistance.
continuation.statusNote: Prototype exploration · The returning auto-quote screens illustrate the broader Auto, Home, and Renters direction. Intended outcomes are not measured results or a claim of shipped AI capabilities.

decisionStory.result: A shopping prototype that makes the assistance model tangible, supported by interface explorations and shared Digital Assistance patterns.

neurotrade.overview: I led research, UX, and UI design for an AI-assisted trading experience, connecting onboarding, exchange setup, bot configuration, and portfolio monitoring. My focus was making complex automation easier to understand and giving people a clearer view of their assets and activity.

decisionStory.title: Complex automation. Clearer decisions.
decisionStory.problem: Trading platforms can overwhelm people with dense information, unfamiliar controls, and uncertainty about AI-driven decisions.
decisionStory.decision: I organized the experience around distinct tasks: understand the portfolio, choose a bot, configure its settings, then monitor its activity.
decisionStory.result: I delivered onboarding flows, dashboard and trading interfaces, AI / DCA / signal-bot screens, and an interactive Figma prototype.

aboutParagraphs: I’m Terry Germany, a senior and principal-level product design leader based in Carrollton, Texas. I bring 25+ years of experience across Apple, Cisco, State Farm, and Scoop News Group.
I connect human–AI interaction, research, and hands-on design with Product and Engineering—making complex systems clear, useful, and trusted.

project.title: Making complex insurance feel human.
project.subtitle: State Farm Digital Assistant + AI — B2C Experience
project.role: Senior Experience Lead, AI & Digital Assistance
project.domain: Focus: AI Experience Strategy · Conversational AI · Generative AI · Agentic Experiences · Research · Product Design · Experience Architecture · Design Systems · Team Leadership
project.challenge:
State Farm had multiple digital journeys, service experiences, and emerging AI initiatives being developed across separate teams. Customers often had to navigate complex forms, disconnected experiences, and traditional task-based interfaces to accomplish relatively simple goals.
The opportunity was to rethink those experiences around an AI-first assistance model—one capable of understanding customer intent, guiding users through complex insurance decisions, completing tasks, explaining recommendations, and escalating to a human when appropriate.
contribution: Led 25+ specialists across Design, Research, Data Science, Engineering, Product, Content, and AI.
Owned strategy across 12+ journeys: SmartQuote, quote review/purchase, service, registration/onboarding, claims/FNOL, and policy/vehicle management.
Directed research, prototypes, experimentation, and the Digital Assistance Design Kit; implemented the Level 1–3 AI Maturity Model with Product and Engineering.
project.evidence: Established shared AI experience principles, reusable interaction patterns, and experience governance across State Farm’s consumer ecosystem. Connected near-term product work with a longer-term roadmap for generative AI, predictive assistance, and emerging agentic experiences.
project.takeaway: AI should help people accomplish a goal while making its behavior understandable. Trust, accessibility, transparency, and human support belong in the interaction model from the start.

digital-assistance.researchIntro: I embedded research in product strategy, partnering with researchers, data scientists, Product, and Engineering to evaluate whether AI felt useful, understandable, trustworthy, and appropriate for the State Farm brand.

Test entry points, CTA language, suggestion chips, proactive assistance, and visual treatments to understand how people discover and use AI.

evidence.title: Research + experimentation
evidence.summary: Research into how customers find, use, and trust digital assistance.
evidence.detail:
I directed research and experimentation with Research, Data Science, Product, and Engineering to understand where digital assistance could make insurance easier. We explored entry points, conversational versus traditional interfaces, proactive help, personalization, AI identity, trust, and human handoff.

The work included prototypes and variations for moderated research and A/B testing. Program data covering 27,700 onboarding and service interactions helped frame the opportunity: 14,612 were resolved without escalation, while 13,088 needed additional support. I used that context to focus the design on clearer guidance and smoother transitions to human help.

evidence.title: AI Maturity Model
evidence.summary: A practical path from Level 1 to Level 3 AI assistance.
evidence.detail:
I implemented the AI Maturity Model with Product and Engineering to give teams a shared way to plan the progression from Level 1 to Level 3. It connected AI capabilities to the customer experience we wanted to create.

Level 1 — Assisted Automation: rules-based help for defined tasks.

Level 2 — Context-Aware AI: assistance that responds to the customer’s situation.

Level 3 — Predictive AI Companion: assistance that anticipates needs and offers proactive guidance.

The model helped align priorities and experience standards across teams. It describes the direction of the work; individual features progressed at different stages.

project.title: Clarity for people running complex work.
project.subtitle: Enterprise platform design spanning event operations, analytical data, and connected workflows.
project.role: Principal Product Designer · AI & Government SaaS
project.challenge: Event and data workflows span speakers, organizations, invitations, content, and publishing. People need to see their next step without understanding the underlying system.
project.evidence: The event-creator and system-alignment work are ongoing design initiatives. Integration concepts and automation plans are distinguished from completed production capabilities.
project.takeaway: A strong enterprise experience makes the next decision obvious, even when the system underneath is complex.

decisions.title: Give creation a clear start
decisions.text: Separated guided event setup from ongoing management: choose a new layout, reuse an existing layout, or save a draft before returning to the operational workspace.

decisions.title: Make complexity navigable
decisions.text: Used AG Grid and contextual panels for operational work, with consistent draft states and deliberate minimize behavior.

decisions.title: Close the design-to-code gap
decisions.text: Worked with engineering on consistency and change tracking across Figma, Storybook, and the repository. Automation remains an evolving workflow.

maturity.contribution: I introduced and implemented the AI Maturity Model with State Farm Product and Engineering, giving teams a shared framework for the progression from Level 1 Assisted Automation to Level 3 Predictive AI Companion.

levels.name: Assisted Automation
levels.summary: The customer asks. The system follows a defined path.
levels.product: Define clear, repeatable assistance for known customer tasks.
levels.engineering: Connect predictable rules and decision paths to the experience.
levels.customer: Useful answers, with the customer initiating each step.
levels.example: How do I get help with my claim?
levels.exampleResponse: Choose the claim topic you need help with, and I’ll guide you to the next step.

levels.name: Context-Aware AI
levels.summary: The system responds with awareness of the customer's situation.
levels.product: Connect assistance to the journey and the customer's immediate need.
levels.engineering: Make the relevant journey context available to the interaction.
levels.customer: Guidance that fits the task instead of restarting from a generic answer.
levels.example: I’m in the middle of a quote. What should I do next?
levels.exampleResponse: Let’s continue from the step you’re on and clarify the information you need.

levels.name: Predictive AI Companion
levels.summary: The experience anticipates a relevant need and offers a next step.
levels.product: Identify moments where anticipation can create useful guidance across insurance journeys.
levels.engineering: Connect signals and context to timely suggestions while preserving customer control.
levels.customer: Relevant help before another question is needed, with a choice about what happens next.
levels.example: A relevant life change could affect your coverage.
levels.exampleResponse: Would you like to review your options? You decide whether to explore the next step.
